title: Mostar education workers' protest walk for pay and work conditions
location: Public route through central Mostar from Gimnazija Mostar to the Herzegovina-Neretva Canton government building
organizer: Herzegovina-Neretva Canton education-worker unions; RFE/RL also identifies representatives of public officials and police unions as participants/organizers
participants_original: Dnevni avaz reports more than 1,000 education workers in HNK primary and secondary schools protested in Mostar. N1 says 1,500 citizens were expected and that a large number gathered; the 1,500 is a forecast, not actual attendance.
participants_precision: reported lower bound; turnout method not given
threshold_50_evidence: Dnevni avaz's contemporaneous article explicitly reports more than 1,000 education workers protesting in Mostar on February 20; N1 and RFE/RL also report the protest walk; editorial independence among these accounts is not established here.

occurrence_and_demands.summary: N1, RFE/RL and Avaz report the February 20 protest walk in Mostar and demands directed to the HNK government, including higher pay, one-time assistance, payment of final court judgments for labor-rights violations and permanent hiring. Avaz reports a 15% pay demand and a one-time payment under a Federation-government decision.

location_and_organizer.summary: Avaz places the public walk from Gimnazija Mostar to the cantonal government; RFE/RL says education, civil-servant and police union representatives from HNK participated. Solidarity visitors from Tuzla and Bihać were reported at the Mostar action and are not separate events.

participants.summary: Avaz directly reports more than 1,000 education workers at the event. N1's expected 1,500 is an advance estimate and is not used as actual turnout.

dates.summary: RFE/RL explicitly dates the walk and image to February 20, 2024; Avaz publication is February 20 and says the event happened that day. No physical end is established.

unknown_responses.summary: Read text does not establish a protest-specific accommodation, arrest, beating, crowd dispersal, ignore, killing or shooting. Avaz reports organizer allegations of pressure before the walk, not confirmed event-time response; responses remain unknown.

notes: A distinct February 20 public gathering, described by RFE/RL as the second walk in two months; it follows a December 18, 2023 walk and December 8 warning strike, but no evidence says the February action was continuous with them. Do not merge with the earlier campaign action. Reports describe one Mostar event with visiting solidarity participants, not separate Tuzla or Bihać gatherings. Official baseline and review remain pending.
open_questions: What specific turnout-counting method underlies Avaz's ‘more than 1,000’ figure, and is it independent from other reporting?
What was the physical end time or end date of the February 20 walk?
Did the HNK government hold any event-specific negotiations or take other responses after the walk? The reports read do not resolve this.
How does the February 20 action relate organizationally to the December 18, 2023 walk? Current reporting describes separate dates and does not establish continuous occupation or action.

title: Tuzla protest walk over Amra Kahrimanović’s killing and police accountability
location: Public walk from the Sjenjak shopping center to a platform near the Tuzla Canton Ministry of Internal Affairs headquarters, Tuzla
organizer: Family and supporters of Amra Kahrimanović; the read RFE/RL text does not name a formal organizer
participants_original: RFE/RL reports that FENA reported more than several thousand participants (BCS: više hiljada); no counting method is given.
participants_precision: qualitative multi-thousand lower bound as attributed by RFE/RL to FENA; no method reported
threshold_50_evidence: RFE/RL reports the walk drew ‘više hiljada ljudi’ (several thousand people), attributed explicitly to FENA, far above the 50-person threshold. The report documents demands for urgent sessions of the Tuzla Canton government and assembly, the interior minister’s removal, disciplinary accountability for officials, and regular medical examinations for police.

occurrence_and_demands.summary: RFE/RL documents a peaceful public walk and quotes demands for urgent government and assembly sessions, ministerial removal, disciplinary accountability of officials, and regular police medical examinations. Coded under political process/accountability and removal of a politician; public service specifics are retained in the narrative.

location_and_organizer.summary: The route passed Sjenjak shopping center and ended near the Tuzla Canton MUP headquarters. Family members were speakers; formal organizing body is not named.

participants.summary: RFE/RL attributes to FENA the report of ‘više hiljada ljudi’ (several thousand). This is a reported lower-bound magnitude, with no counting method or independent count in the source.

dates.summary: Article headline/date and image caption explicitly date the event to 11 February 2024. The article says the walk ended in quiet, the physical end date was the same day.

unknown_responses.summary: No protest-specific state response is reported. Tuzla’s declared day of mourning is contextual and not coded as accommodation to the protest. The article records demands and a seven-day deadline, with no later official response in the read text.

notes: Domestic competent-authority demands are explicit and distinct from the homicide as a private crime: protestors called on Tuzla Canton government/assembly and MUP leadership for personnel changes, accountability, and improved police medical examination policy. Do not merge this gathering with later rallies solely because they share the same case. Official baseline/review pending.
open_questions: How did FENA establish the reported several-thousand turnout; are independent contemporaneous sources available?
Did the Tuzla Canton government or assembly respond to the seven-day deadline after the gathering?
Was there a formally named organizer beyond the victim’s family and supporters?
Does the BCS plural ‘više hiljada’ justify a formal minimum of 2,000 under the coding convention?
